scope: This is a provenance and research-audit catalogue. A named entry is not a recommendation, routine step, product match, dose, frequency, suitability decision, or treatment claim.

selectionPolicy.rationale: The only linked evidence evaluates a product-specific, multi-ingredient cream-plus-cleanser regimen. It cannot attribute outcomes or safety to any one listed ingredient or authorize named-ingredient routine selection.

limitations: The linked study evaluated a combined tested regimen, not any ingredient alone or a generic product containing one of these names.
The study involved 100 adults with clinician-diagnosed moderate eczema at one Australian centre; it does not establish results for other concerns, locations, ages, or consumer self-selection.
The intervention lasted 28 days, so it does not establish long-term or universal safety.
The study excluded people with known reactions to the tested moisturizer or its components; a short trial does not establish individual tolerance.
Six study authors were employees of the manufacturer or sponsor, so the conflict disclosure remains attached to every candidate.
The reported between-group EASI difference was not significant; the catalogue must not be used to claim that the listed ingredients treat eczema or improve disease severity.

evidenceRecords.title: A daily regimen of a ceramide-dominant moisturizing cream and cleanser restores the skin permeability barrier in adults with moderate eczema: A randomized trial
evidenceRecords.citation: Spada F et al. A daily regimen of a ceramide-dominant moisturizing cream and cleanser restores the skin permeability barrier in adults with moderate eczema: A randomized trial. Dermatologic Therapy. 2021. doi:10.1111/dth.14970.
evidenceRecords.populationScope: 100 adults with clinician-diagnosed moderate eczema at one Australian centre
evidenceRecords.interventionScope: A specific active cream-plus-cleanser regimen; this catalogue does not identify or recommend a product.
evidenceRecords.conflictDisclosure: Six authors were employees of the manufacturer or sponsor.
outcomeContext: The combined active regimen showed greater improvement than placebo in transepidermal water loss and skin-hydration measures.
The between-group difference in EASI was not significant.
A small share of the active group reported treatment-related stinging or pain; this is not proof of universal safety.
limitations: Product-specific, multi-ingredient regimen; effects cannot be attributed to a single ingredient.
Short, single-centre adult moderate-eczema study; it is not a generic barrier-care or consumer-routine trial.
Known moisturizer/component reactions were an exclusion criterion, and sponsor employment conflicts were recorded.
